name: Gough and Inaccessible Islands
countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
description: Gough and Inaccessible Islands are two remote volcanic islands in the South Atlantic, part of the UK's Tristan da Cunha group and about 2,700 km west of Cape Town. Sheer cliffs rise straight from the ocean, and because no introduced mammals live here, millions of seabirds nest undisturbed. Each island also shelters its own unique land birds, plants and invertebrates. Gough's only residents are a small weather-station crew.
